text: Make executable:
code: # configure (macOS/Linux/Windows) #!/bin/sh set -e : "${R_HOME:=$(R RHOME)}" VTK_CPPFLAGS="$("${R_HOME}/bin/Rscript" --vanilla -e "rvtk::CppFlags()")" # LdFlagsFile() writes all linker flags to a response file (src/vtk_libs.rsp) # and returns the short token @vtk_libs.rsp that is safe on all platforms, # including Windows where the full flag string can exceed the 8191-char limit. VTK_LIBS="$("${R_HOME}/bin/Rscript" --vanilla -e "rvtk::LdFlagsFile('src/vtk_libs.rsp')")" sed -e "s|@VTK_CPPFLAGS@|${VTK_CPPFLAGS}|g" \     -e "s|@VTK_LIBS@|${VTK_LIBS}|g" \     src/Makevars.in > src/Makevars # configure.win (Windows) #!/bin/sh ./configure chmod +x configure configure.win

title: rvtk 0.1.1
text: planned CRAN submission v0.1.0 cancelled downstream package developers reported linker errors building pre-built Windows VTK libraries. Two root causes identified fixed: Wrong toolchain. Windows VTK zip compiled Rtools45 UCRT64 toolchain (/ucrt64/bin/gcc), uses dynamic C runtime emits DLL-import symbols (__imp_fseeko64, __imp_ftello64, …). However, R CMD INSTALL links R packages x86_64-w64-mingw32.static.posix toolchain, fully static. mismatch caused undefined references nanosleep64, ftime64, __imp_fseeko64, __imp_ftello64. GitHub Actions workflow now builds Windows VTK zip x86_64-w64-mingw32.static.posix compiler, matching toolchain downstream packages use. Command-line length overflow. full set VTK -l linker flags exceeds 8 191-character Windows command-line limit, causing linker silently drop flags end list. new function LdFlagsFile(path) writes flags response file returns short @path token GNU ld LLVM lld support. Downstream packages call LdFlagsFile('src/vtk_libs.rsp') configure / configure.win script instead LdFlags().

Windows system libraries appended PKG_LIBS reduced -lgdi32 ; UCRT64-specific -lwinpthread -lmingwex -lucrtbase flags longer needed static.posix sysroot resolves POSIX symbols internally. README updated document LdFlagsFile(), explain rationale, provide unified configure example valid platforms, correct Windows toolchain description.
